issues.body: `Num::of_literal` trims numeric lexical forms before parsing, reflecting the XSD numeric datatypes' whitespace-collapse behavior, but `integer_facets_ok` and `exact_decimal_lexical` pass the original untrimmed `lex` to `cmp_plain_decimal`. Thus a valid pair such as `" 1 "^^xsd:positiveInteger = "1"^^xsd:integer` fails the facet check and returns `DistinctGroundEqual`. Likewise, an out-of-i128 `xsd:integer` or `xsd:decimal` surrounded by whitespace is rejected by the exact fallback. This contradicts the module and skill claims that both well-formed numeric operands are decided and reintroduces the documented whitespace-padded numeric acceptance-set mismatch class.
issues.fix_hint: Apply the datatype's whitespace normalization consistently before facet validation and exact-decimal comparison (at minimum use the same trimmed lexical that `Num::of_literal` parses), while preserving rejection of internal whitespace and invalid integer fraction/exponent forms. Add real `validate` and `closure` tests for whitespace-padded derived-integer boundaries and whitespace-padded >i128 integer/decimal equality and inequality controls.
issues.title: Raw lexical comparisons reject valid whitespace-collapsed numeric literals

verdict.summary: Round 3 fixes the prior derived-integer facet bug with explicit arbitrary-precision bounds checks and adds meaningful validation/closure tests for invalid and boundary values. However, the new paths compare raw lexical strings while the shared numeric classifier applies the XSD whitespace-collapse behavior via trim(). Consequently valid whitespace-padded derived integers and out-of-i128 integer/decimal values are rejected as undecidable, despite the new public documentation claiming all well-formed numeric pairs are decided. This is a new major correctness/completeness finding, so progress is regressing under the required rubric.
